sources.entry: oh-my-patent by illusionaireal - A plugin for turning technical ideas into patent disclosures.

summary.one_liner: A patent workflow toolkit that runs as a plugin or portable Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, using a multi-agent orchestrator (Archimedes) to turn technical ideas into patent disclosures.
summary.what_it_does: Provides an orchestrator called Archimedes that coordinates 14 specialist agents across research, ideation, patentability assessment, drafting, review, and technical responses. The README describes a ten-stage workflow from INIT through RESEARCH, brainstorm rounds, DRAFT, diagram drafting, QA loop, final review, and DONE, with review loops that can return to earlier stages. It records decisions in a .brainstorm/ directory (rounds, scores, innovation snapshots) so branches can be compared or restored, and keeps workflow state in .patent/state.json. It can generate patent figures as specifications and editable SVG, with optional local rendering or approved host image tools. A CLI provides project queries, Markdown reports, a terminal UI, and environment checks.
use_cases: Drafting a patent disclosure from a technical idea
Running prior-art style research for an invention
Generating patent figures and SVG diagrams
Reviewing and revising patent drafts through QA loops
Tracking and branching invention brainstorming decisions
Resuming an in-progress patent project with saved context
notable: Ships as both a host plugin (14 agents, 6 skills, 9 commands) and a self-contained portable Agent Skill
Traceable decision history: saved brainstorm rounds, scores and snapshots that can be branched or restored
Figure pipeline with fallbacks: saved local choice, local renderer, then direct SVG, with human acceptance required for final figures
Adversarial brainstorming where candidate ideas get examiner-style challenges before selection
caveats: Requires Node.js 22 or later; Skill installation via the Skills CLI also needs Git
Research depends on an available retrieval source; academic-only retrieval requires explicit acceptance of its limits, and MCP servers need a host-tool check
Rendering engines and retrieval services have their own setup requirements, described in the usage guide
